title: Prefill/decode disaggregation: separate servers for the two phases, with the KV cache moved between them
design_ref: Prefill/decode disaggregation: when it pays and what it costs
purpose: On a prompt-heavy mix, run four unified servers, and then two prefill + two decode servers and one prefill + three decode servers joined by NIXL; verify that the KV cache really moved, and compare goodput per GPU and latency.

checks.description: pd2p2d: the KV cache moved between servers: transfers happened, none failed, and the decode servers took most of their prompt from them
checks.because: 100% of the decode servers' prompt tokens were found through the connector rather than computed. Prefill servers generated 1,635 tokens (one per request, the trigger) and decode servers 159,442: the two phases ran where they were placed.

checks.description: pd1p3d: the KV cache moved between servers: transfers happened, none failed, and the decode servers took most of their prompt from them
checks.because: 100% of the decode servers' prompt tokens were found through the connector rather than computed. Prefill servers generated 1,635 tokens (one per request, the trigger) and decode servers 159,442: the two phases ran where they were placed.

checks.description: every layout served its lightest level completely (at least 95% of requests finished), so the curves are comparable
checks.because: Whether a layout meets the targets is the result; that it ran is the precondition.

notes: Layouts that never kept 95% of requests inside their targets, even at the lightest level (0.3 req/s per GPU): pd1p3d. For 1P+3D the cause is in the table above: one prefill GPU computes every prompt (70% of them 1,300 tokens), so first-token waits are several seconds before the transfer even starts.

PREDICTED: separating the phases removes prompt work from the decode servers' steps, so inter-token latency at the same load is lower with disaggregation. MEASURED chat ITL p95 at 0.6 req/s per GPU: unified 159 ms, 2P+2D 92 ms, 1P+3D 62 ms. The prediction held.

PREDICTED: on four GPUs that share one PCIe fabric and have no GPU-direct path between pods, the transfer and the idle half of the node cost more than the interference they remove, so unified wins on goodput per GPU. MEASURED best: unified. The prediction held.
